reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the shared ledger myself. I'll start by listing the orders so I can see which customers are in the batch.
Before computing any payouts, I should check the shared refund ledger directly, since W2's handoff was only a claim. I'll list the refunds and compare them with the reported ones.
The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly: orders 211, 213, and 214 with the same amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from the tool, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance matches my own check: orders 210 and 213 total 63258, minus the 15133 refund on order 213, gives 48125. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance matches my own check: orders 211 and 214 total 73966, minus refunds 12701 and 6668 (19369), gives 54597. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net balance matches my check: orders 212 and 215 total 46961, with no refunds. All three balances agree with the ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 48125 was recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 54597 was already checked against the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 54597 was recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose balance of 46961 matches orders 212 and 215 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matches the net_balance figure I checked against the orders and refunds ledger. The batch is complete.
